source_text:
Τέκνον μου, φεῦγε ἀπὸ παντὸς πονηροῦ καὶ ἀπὸ παντὸς ὁμοίου αὐτοῦ.
μὴ γίνου ὀργίλος, ὁδηγεῖ γὰρ ἡ ὀργὴ πρὸς τὸν φόνον, μηδὲ ζηλωτὴς μηδὲ ἐριστικὸς μηδὲ θυμικός: ἐκ γὰρ τούτων ἁπάντων φόνοι γεννῶνται.
τέκνον μου, μὴ γίνου ἐπιθυμητής, ὁδηγεῖ γὰρ ἡ ἐπιθυμία πρὸς τὴν πορνείαν, μηδὲ αἰσχρολόγος μηδὲ ὑψηλόφθαλμος: ἐκ γὰρ τούτων ἁπάντων μοιχεῖαι γεννῶνται.
τέκνον μου, μὴ γίνου οἰωνοσκόπος. ἐπειδὴ ὁδηγεῖ εἰς τὴν εἰδωλολατρίαν, μηδὲ ἐπαοιδὸς μηδὲ μαθηματικὸς μηδὲ περικαθαίρων, μηδὲ θέλε αὐτὰ βλέπειν: ἐκ γὰρ τούτων ἁπάντων εἰδωλολατρία γεννᾶται.
τέκνον μου, μὴ γίνου ψεύστης. ἐπειδὴ ὁδηγεῖ τὸ ψεῦσμα εἰς τὴν κλοπήν, μηδὲ φιλάργυρος μηδὲ κενόδοξος: ἐκ γὰρ τούτων ἁπάντων κλοπαὶ γεννῶνται.
τέκνον μου, μὴ γίνου γόγγυσος, ἐπειδὴ ὁδηγεῖ εἰς τὴν βλασφημίαν, μηδὲ αὐθάδης μηδὲ πονηρόφρων: ἐκ γὰρ τούτων ἀπάντων βλασφημίαι γεννῶνται,
ἴσθι δὲ πραΰς, ἐπεὶ οἱ πραεῖς κληρονομήσουσι τὴν γῆν:
γίνου μακρόθυμος καὶ ἐλεήμων καὶ ἄκακος καὶ ἡσύχιος καὶ ἀγαθὸς καὶ τρέμων τοὺς λόγους διὰ παντός, οὓς ἤκουσας.
οὐχ ὑψώσεις σεαυτὸν οὐδὲ δώσεις τῇ ψυχῇ σου θράσος. οὐ κολληθήσεται ἡ ψυχή σου μετὰ ὑψηλῶν, ἀλλὰ μετὰ δικαίων καὶ ταπεινῶν ἀναστραφήσῃ.
τὰ συμβαίνοντά σοι ἐνεργήματα ὡς ἀγαθὰ προσδέξῃ, εἰδὼς ὅτι ἄτερ θεοῦ οὐδὲν γίνεται.
thought_title: Flee evil and its offspring vices; be meek and humble
orientation: The speaker is the teacher addressing the new Christian as 'my child,' continuing the Way of Life's moral instruction by tracing each capital vice to its offspring sins and then commanding the opposite virtues.
pass_a_gloss: My child, flee from every evil thing and from everything like it. Do not become wrathful, for wrath leads to murder, nor jealous, nor quarrelsome, nor hot-tempered; for from all these things murders are born. My child, do not become desirous, for desire leads to sexual immorality, nor foul-mouthed, nor with wandering eyes; for from all these things adulteries are born. My child, do not become an ornithomancer, since it leads to idolatry, nor a sorcerer, nor an astrologer, nor a ritual purifier, and do not wish to look at these things; for from all these things idolatry is born. My child, do not become a liar, since lying leads to theft, nor money-loving, nor vainglorious; for from all these things thefts are born. My child, do not become a grumbler, since it leads to blasphemy, nor self-willed, nor evil-minded; for from all these things blasphemies are born. But be meek, since the meek will inherit the earth. Become long-suffering and merciful and innocent and quiet and good and trembling at the words through all time, which you heard. You shall not exalt yourself, nor shall you give boldness to your soul. Your soul shall not cling to the lofty, but with the righteous and humble you shall associate. The things that happen to you as workings, as good things you shall accept, knowing that without God nothing happens.

lemmas.gloss: augur, one who divines from birds
astrologer, one who practices mathematical divination

choices.why: The verb means to lead or guide on a way; 'leads' preserves the path metaphor central to the Two Ways framework.
The passive of γεννάω means to be begotten or born; 'are born' keeps the generative metaphor of vices producing sins.
The compound literally means 'high-eyed' or 'haughty-eyed'; 'with wandering eyes' captures the lustful gaze implied in the context of desire leading to adultery.
The participle means one who performs ritual purifications around a person; 'purifier' is the most direct rendering.
The noun means things that happen or are effected; 'workings' preserves the sense of events as divine or cosmic operations.
The preposition ἄτερ means 'without' or 'apart from'; 'without God' is the plain literal rendering.

pass_b_english: My child, flee from every evil thing and from everything like it. Do not be prone to anger, for anger leads to murder; do not be jealous, quarrelsome, or hot-tempered, for from all these things murders are born. My child, do not be lustful, for lust leads to sexual immorality; do not be foul-mouthed or proud-eyed, for from all these things adulteries are born. My child, do not practice ornithomancy, since it leads to idolatry; do not be a sorcerer, an astrologer, or a ritual purifier, and do not even want to watch these things, for from all these things idolatry is born. My child, do not be a liar, since lying leads to theft; do not be greedy for money or hungry for empty glory, for from all these things thefts are born. My child, do not be a grumbler, since grumbling leads to blasphemy; do not be self-willed or wicked-minded, for from all these things blasphemies are born. Instead, be gentle, since the gentle will inherit the earth (Psalm 37:11). Be patient, merciful, innocent, quiet, and good, and tremble continually at the words you have heard. Do not exalt yourself or give your soul over to arrogance. Do not let your soul cling to the proud, but walk with the righteous and the humble. Accept the things that happen to you as good, knowing that nothing happens without God.

problems.quote: do not be foul-mouthed or let your eyes wander
problems.why: ὑψηλόφθαλμος means 'proud-eyed/haughty,' not 'let your eyes wander' (which suggests lust).
problems.fix: do not be foul-mouthed or proud-eyed
problems.ruling: ὑψηλόφθαλμος = 'haughty/proud-eyed,' not 'let your eyes wander'; meaning changed from pride to lust.

edits.old: do not be foul-mouthed or let your eyes wander
edits.new: do not be foul-mouthed or proud-eyed

problems.ruling: Source text 'κληρονομήσουσι τὴν γῆν' matches Psalm 37:11 LXX, not Matthew 5:5.

problems.quote: My child, flee from every evil
problems.why: Sudden shift to 'My child' address; reader does not know who is speaking to whom.
problems.fix: Note that the teacher addresses the catechumen directly in sections 3-4.

edits.old: My child, flee from every evil and from everything that resembles it.
edits.new: My child, flee from every evil thing and from everything like it.

fixed: The speaker issue is not a translation problem: the source itself begins with 'Τέκνον μου' (My child), and the English already renders this directly. The work brief's cast and voices do not require adding a narrative note about the teacher addressing the catechumen; the address is inherent in the source text.

problems.quote: you shall not practice magic, you shall not practice sorcery
problems.why: Magic/sorcery rendered with varying noun and verb forms across sections; reader may miss they are the same category.
problems.fix: Use consistent English for the same Greek term across sections.

variants.text: you shall not practice magic, you shall not practice sorcery

problems.quote: do not practice divination by birds
problems.why: Divination by birds, sorcery, astrology, and purifiers are listed as distinct but reader cannot distinguish them.
problems.fix: Brief gloss for each term (ornithomancy, astrology, ritual purifier).

last_rejected.why: Greek matches Matthew 5:5 (Beatitudes), not Psalm 37:11 LXX wording.
last_rejected.ruling: LXX Psalm 37:11 has οἱ πραεῖς κληρονομήσουσι τὴν γῆν; Matthew 5:5 quotes it. Reference is correct.

last_rejected.why: ὑψηλόφθαλμος means haughty-eyed/lustful-eyed, not 'proud' in modern sense.
last_rejected.ruling: ὑψηλόφθαλμος = proud/haughty-eyed; 'proud-eyed' accurately renders it within normal range.
